# Sampling {.unnumbered}

```{r set}
#| include: false
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(flextable)
library(scales)
```


```{r data}
#| message: false
# inventory
inventory <- readxl::read_excel("data/raw/inventory/inventory_Belterra_20260618.xlsx",
                                sheet = "22092026") %>% 
  select(PLACA, NOME_COMUM, NOME_CIENTIFICO, FAMILIA, 
         CAP1, CAP2, CAP3, CAP4, CAP5, CAP6, CAP7, E, N) %>% 
  mutate(across(num_range("CAP", 1:7), as.numeric)) %>% 
  rename(tree = PLACA,
         vernacular = NOME_COMUM,
         botanical = NOME_CIENTIFICO,
         family = FAMILIA,
         x_utm = E,
         y_utm = N) %>% 
  mutate(botanical = str_extract(botanical, "^\\S+\\s+\\S+"), 
         bota_code = paste0(
           str_sub(word(botanical, 1), 1, 2),
           str_sub(word(botanical, 2), 1, 2)),
         label = paste0(bota_code, "_", tree),
         botanical = replace_values(botanical, "Byrsonima crassifólia" ~ "Byrsonima crassifolia"),
         bota_code = replace_values(bota_code, "NANA" ~ NA)) %>% 
  rowwise() %>% 
  mutate(dbh = max(CAP1, CAP2, CAP3, CAP4, CAP5, CAP6, CAP7)/pi) %>% 
  select(tree, x_utm, y_utm, 
         vernacular, botanical, family, bota_code, label, dbh) %>% 
  ungroup() # to remove row_wise

# inventory %>% group_by(bota_code) %>% summarise(n = n_distinct(botanical)) %>% filter(n>1)

# spatial object
spat_file <- "data/raw/geographic/inventory_Belterra_20260922.gpkg"
roads <- read_sf(spat_file, "EstradasdoPPesquisa")
path <- read_sf(spat_file, "TrilhaParqPesq")
inventory <- inventory %>% 
  st_as_sf(coords = c("x_utm", "y_utm"), crs = 31981)

n_tree_tot <- length(unique(inventory$tree))
```

These sampling choices are made considering the inventory data of the 22/09/2026.
This inventory contains `r n_tree_tot` individuals <!-- one duplicaed tree ID but for pinus --> .
For multistemed trees, we consider only the DBH of the bigger stem.

Unlike in 2025, the sampling is decided based on the botanical names
(as identification as occurred since). 
There are `r n_distinct(inventory$botanical, na.rm=TRUE)` different species,
with `r inventory %>% filter(is.na(botanical)) %>% nrow()` unidentified tree.
We add a botanical code using the two first letters of the genus and species.
We also add a label using the botanical code and the tree ID, that will be used for sampling.
*NB: in the field, only the tree ID is displayed on the trees.*

We also use 

* the version 1 of cleaned leaf trait data from [field campaign of 2025](20_belterra25/26_junction)

* the list of the wood core taken in 2025. *NB: some cores may not be measured if Romain thinks they are not good enough. We will revise all the wood core with Romain on the first day of fieldwork, and add the trees with bad quality core to the sampling objective. 

* the list of planted species


```{r}
#| message: false
meas_2025 <- read_csv("outputs/trait_PlantForAdapt_Belterra_2025_v1.csv") %>% 
  mutate(botanical = str_extract(botanical, "^\\S+\\s+\\S+")) %>% 
  group_by(tree, botanical, verna_code) %>% 
  summarise(n_la_2025 = sum(!is.na(la)),
            n_ldmc_2025 = sum(!is.na(ldmc)),
            n_lt_2025 = sum(!is.na(lt)),
            n_sla_2025 = sum(!is.na(sla)),
            n_tlp_2025 = sum(!is.na(tlp))) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  rowwise() %>% # remove the one that have 0 for all traits, if any
  mutate(n_leaf = sum(n_la_2025, n_ldmc_2025, n_lt_2025, n_sla_2025, n_tlp_2025)) %>% 
  filter(n_leaf != 0) %>% 
  select(-n_leaf)
inventory <- inventory %>% 
  left_join(meas_2025)

wd_2025 <- readxl::read_excel("data/raw/Belterra_2025/sample_taken.xlsx",
                                sheet = "Feuil1",
                             na = c("", "NA")) %>%
  rename(tree = ID,
         verna_code = Species) %>% 
  mutate(verna_code = replace_values(verna_code, "VIROLA" ~ "VIROL"),
         Wood1 = ifelse(is.na(Wood1), 0, Wood1),
         Wood2 = ifelse(is.na(Wood2), 0, Wood2)) %>% 
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(n_core_2025 = sum(c(Wood1,Wood2), na.rm=T)) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  filter(n_core_2025 != 0) %>% 
  select(verna_code, tree, n_core_2025) 
inventory <- inventory %>% 
  left_join(wd_2025, by = "tree") %>% 
  mutate(verna_code = coalesce(verna_code.x, verna_code.y)) %>% 
  select(-verna_code.x, -verna_code.y)

planted <- readxl::read_excel("data/raw/inventory/planted_sp_Belterra.xlsx",
                              sheet = "planted_sp_Belterra",
                              na = c("", "NA")) %>% 
  mutate(across(c(planted, ppd_sen, native) , as.logical))
  
inventory <- inventory %>% 
  left_join(planted)
```


## Objective

The functional traits will be used to:

* characterize the ecological strategies of native tree species in order to explain species demography and response to climate (T1.1)

* predict the outcome of species interactions on tree performances under drought (T2.1)

For the first objectives, we can focus in the planted species, 
but for the second, covering as much as possible the diversity of all species (planted or naturally regenerating) is important.
We will therefore aim to sample  all the planted species, and non-planted species representing the highest proportion of the stem number that we can achieve.

We will sample on minimum of 5 trees per species and per sites to account for intraspecific variability. 
However, to minimise the effect of ontogentic trait variations, we will standardise this by sampling on the biggest individuals (as a proxy for the tallest).
[TO DO: check for non-planted species that we are not sampling on too yound individuals.]{style="color: red;"}

The traits to measure are listed on this [page](11_traits), on 5 leaves per individual, except for TLP for which we take only two leaves and [Gmin]{style="color: red;"}.
For wood density, we take two wood cores per individual.

This second field campaign in Belterra aims at complementing the [field campaign of 2025](20_belterra25).


```{r}
#| warning: false
ggplot() +

  geom_sf(data = path) +
```

Maps of the native versus exotic species:

```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = roads) +
  geom_sf(data = path) +
  geom_sf(data = inventory, aes(col = native), size = 0.5) +
  theme_bw() + 
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

As the exotic species are not mixed with the native ones, we don't need to sample traits on them (even for calculating neighbourhood indices).

## Species choice among the not already sampled one

Here we consider that a species has not been sampled if it was neither sampled for leaf nor for wood.

```{r}
sampl_leaf_2025 <- inventory %>% 
  filter(if_any(c(n_la_2025, n_ldmc_2025, n_lt_2025, n_sla_2025, n_tlp_2025),
                ~ .x != 0)) %>% 
  distinct(botanical) %>% 
  pull(botanical)

sampl_core_2025 <- inventory %>% 
  filter(n_core_2025 != 0) %>%  
  distinct(botanical) %>% 
  pull(botanical)

abd <- inventory %>% 
  st_drop_geometry() %>% 
  filter(!is.na(botanical)) %>% 
  count(botanical, bota_code, planted, ppd_sen, native) %>% 
  arrange(desc(n)) %>% 
  mutate(prop = n/n_tree_tot,
         cum_prop = cumsum(prop),
         sampled_2025 = case_when(
           (botanical %in% sampl_leaf_2025 & 
             botanical %in% sampl_core_2025) ~ "both",
           (botanical %in% sampl_leaf_2025 & 
             !(botanical %in% sampl_core_2025)) ~ "leaf",
           (!(botanical %in% sampl_leaf_2025) & 
             botanical %in% sampl_core_2025) ~ "wood",
            .default = "none"))
```


### Planted

The graph below show the abundance of native species that were planted (red dashed line indicates a number of individuals currently alive of 50).
As the exotic species are not mixed with the native ones, we don't consider them (even for studying the neighbourhood) so we won't sample them.

```{r}
abd %>% 
  filter(planted == TRUE & native == TRUE) %>% 
  mutate(botanical = fct_reorder(botanical, n)) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = n, y =  botanical, 
             fill = sampled_2025, col = ppd_sen)) + 
  geom_col(linewidth = 1) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("leaf" = "forestgreen", "wood" = "brown",
                               "both" = "blue" , "none" = "grey70")) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "black", `FALSE` = NA)) + 
  geom_vline(xintercept=50, linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.5, col = "red") + 
  theme_minimal()
```
```{r}
# create a table of species to sample
sampling_sp <- abd %>% 
  filter(planted == TRUE & native == TRUE & sampled_2025 == "none" & n>= 50) %>% 
  select(botanical, bota_code, planted, sampled_2025, n) %>% 
  mutate(n_ind_leaf = 5,
         n_ind_wood = 5)
```

> Proposition 1:
Sample all the native species that were planted, that currently have at least 50 living individuals and that were not sampled in 2025.
This concerns the `r nrow(sampling_sp)` following species (n_ind_leaf/wood is the number of individuals to sample for leaf/wood, while n is the total number of living trees) : 

```{r}
sampling_sp %>% 
  flextable() %>% 
  autofit()
```

*We could consider lowering the cutoff of 50, but the 3 most abundant ones with less than 50 tress are the following:*

```{r}
abd %>% 
  filter(planted == TRUE & native == TRUE & sampled_2025 == "none" & n < 50) %>% 
  slice_head(n = 3) %>% 
  flextable() %>% 
  autofit()
```

### Non-planted

```{r}
# nb of indiv of the species with > 0.9 of proportion cumulated
cutoff_prop <- abd %>% filter(cum_prop > 0.9) %>% slice_max(n) %>% pull(n)
```


The graph below show the abundance of species that were not planted: red dashed line indicates a number of individuals currently alive of 50 and the purple dashed line indicates a cut-off corresponding to a cumulative proportion of trees of 90%.
We assume that all the non-planted species are native [Lucas, Jessica, what do you think ? This can be checked if necessary.]{style="color: red;"}


```{r}
abd %>% 
  filter(planted == FALSE) %>% 
  mutate(botanical = fct_reorder(botanical, n)) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = n, y =  botanical, 
             fill = sampled_2025, col = ppd_sen)) + 
  geom_col(linewidth = 1) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("leaf" = "forestgreen", "wood" = "brown",
                               "both" = "blue" , "none" = "grey70")) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "black", `FALSE` = NA)) + 
  geom_vline(xintercept=50, linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.5, col = "red") + 
  geom_vline(xintercept=cutoff_prop, linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.5, col = "purple") + 
  theme_minimal()
```


```{r}
# create a table of species to sample
sampling_no_plant <- abd %>% 
  filter(planted == FALSE & sampled_2025 == "none" & n>= 50) %>% 
  select(botanical, bota_code, planted, sampled_2025, n) %>% 
  mutate(n_ind_leaf = 5,
         n_ind_wood = 5)
sampling_sp <- rbind(sampling_sp, sampling_no_plant)
```

> Proposition 2:
Sample all the non-planted species that currently have at least 50 living individuals and that were not sampled in 2025.
This concerns the `r nrow(sampling_no_plant)` following species : 

```{r}
sampling_no_plant %>% 
  flextable() %>% 
  autofit()
```


*We could consider lowering the cutoff of 50, the 5 most abundant ones with less than 50 tress are the following:*

```{r}
abd %>% 
  filter(planted == FALSE & sampled_2025 == "none" & n < 50) %>% 
  slice_head(n = 5) %>% 
  flextable() %>% 
  autofit()
```


### Choice of the individuals to sample on for these selected species

As the targeted number of individuals per species is 5, 
we pre-select the 10 biggest individuals of the selected species, 
to have a bit of flexibility in the choice of the individuals.

```{r}
sampling_ind <- inventory %>% 
  filter(botanical %in% sampling_sp$botanical) %>% 
  group_by(botanical) %>% 
  top_n(10, dbh) %>% 
  select(tree, botanical, bota_code, label, dbh) %>% 
  mutate(n_leaf = 5,
         n_wood = 2,
         type_sp = "new_sp",
         type_ind = "optional") 
# 121 as two trees with the same DBH
```


## Complementing 2025 campaign

> Proposition 3: we complement all the species that have been sampled in 2025, no matter how many living individuals they have, to have a full dataset. 
We complement both species with not enought individuals, and individuals with not enought leaves or wood cores.

### Not enough individuals

Number of individuals with a least one leaf with a valid trait measurement and/or at least one wood core, per species and per trait:

```{r}
pal <- col_numeric(c("tomato", "gold", "forestgreen"), domain = c(0, 5))

meas_ind <- inventory %>%   
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  rowwise() %>% 
  filter(sum(n_la_2025, n_ldmc_2025, n_lt_2025, n_sla_2025, 
             n_tlp_2025, n_core_2025, 
             na.rm = TRUE) > 0) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  group_by(botanical) %>%
  summarise(across(c(n_la_2025, n_ldmc_2025, n_lt_2025, n_sla_2025, n_tlp_2025, n_core_2025),
                   ~ sum(.x != 0, na.rm = TRUE)),
            .groups = "drop") %>% 
  left_join(select(abd, botanical, bota_code, planted, ppd_sen, sampled_2025, n), by = "botanical")

meas_ind %>% 
  select(-bota_code, -sampled_2025) %>% 
  flextable() %>% 
  bg(j = c("n_la_2025", "n_ldmc_2025", "n_lt_2025", "n_sla_2025", "n_tlp_2025", "n_core_2025"),
     bg = function(x) pal(pmin(x, 5)),
     part = "body") %>% 
  autofit()
```

*NB: Vochysia maxima has 10 individuals because it was sampled under two different vernacular names.*

> Proposition 4: although we want to complement all the species that have been sampled in 2025, we choose not to sample *Enterolobium schuburkii* and *Robrichia schomburgkii* that have very little individuals and very little samples taken in 2025:

```{r}
sampling_suppl <- meas_ind %>% 
  rowwise() %>% 
  mutate(n_ind_leaf = 5 - mean(n_la_2025, n_ldmc_2025, n_lt_2025, n_sla_2025, n_tlp_2025), # change max to mean
         n_ind_wood = 5 - n_core_2025) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  mutate(n_ind_leaf = ifelse(n_ind_leaf <0 , 0, n_ind_leaf),
         n_ind_wood = ifelse(n_ind_wood <0 , 0, n_ind_wood)) %>% 
  filter ((n_ind_leaf > 0 | n_ind_wood > 0) & 
            !(botanical %in% c("Enterolobium schuburkii", "Robrichia schomburgkii"))) %>% 
  select(botanical, bota_code, planted, sampled_2025, n, n_ind_leaf, n_ind_wood) 
sampling_sp <- rbind(sampling_sp, sampling_suppl)
sampling_suppl %>% 
  flextable() %>% 
  autofit()
```

For these species that don't have enough individuals, we select in priorities the individuals on which we have some measurements (leaf or wood), otherwise we select the 8 bigger ones: 

```{r}
# species that need some indiv for leaves but nothing wood:
supl1 <- sampling_suppl %>% 
  filter(n_ind_leaf > 0  & n_ind_wood == 0) 
sampling_supl1 <- inventory %>%
  filter(botanical %in% supl1$botanical &
           (n_la_2025 == 0 | is.na(n_la_2025)) &
           !(n_core_2025 == 0 | is.na(n_core_2025))) %>% 
  select(tree, botanical, bota_code, label, dbh) %>%
  left_join(supl1 %>% select(botanical, n_ind_leaf), by = "botanical") %>%
  group_by(botanical) %>% 
  slice_sample(prop = 1) %>%                      # shuffles the rows within each botanical
  filter(row_number() <= first(n_ind_leaf)) %>%   # keeps the first n per botanical
  ungroup() %>% 
  mutate(n_leaf = 5,
         n_wood = 0,
         type_sp = "compl_sp",
         type_ind = "compulsory") %>% 
  select(-n_ind_leaf)

# species that need some indiv for wood but nothing leaf:
supl2 <- sampling_suppl %>% 
  filter(n_ind_leaf == 0  & n_ind_wood > 0)
sampling_supl2 <- inventory %>%
  filter(botanical %in% supl2$botanical &
           (n_core_2025 == 0 | is.na(n_core_2025)) &
           !(n_la_2025 == 0 | is.na(n_la_2025))) %>% 
  select(tree, botanical, bota_code, label, dbh) %>%
  left_join(supl2 %>% select(botanical, n_ind_wood), by = "botanical") %>%
  group_by(botanical) %>% 
  slice_sample(prop = 1) %>%                      # shuffles the rows within each botanical
  filter(row_number() <= first(n_ind_wood)) %>%   # keeps the first n per botanical
  ungroup() %>% 
  mutate(n_leaf = 0,
         n_wood = 2,
         type_sp = "compl_sp",
         type_ind = "compulsory") %>% 
  select(-n_ind_wood)

# species that need some indiv for both:
supl3 <- sampling_suppl %>% 
  filter(n_ind_leaf > 0  & n_ind_wood > 0)
# first get those that have been sampled for at least one
sampling_supl3.1 <- inventory %>%
  filter(botanical %in% supl3$botanical &
           (n_core_2025 == 0 | is.na(n_core_2025)) &
           !(n_la_2025 == 0 | is.na(n_la_2025)))   %>%  # without core but with la
           select(tree, botanical, bota_code, label, dbh) %>%
  mutate(n_leaf = 0,
         n_wood = 2,
         type_sp = "compl_sp",
         type_ind = "compulsory") 
sampling_supl3.2 <- inventory %>%
  filter(botanical %in% supl3$botanical &
           (n_la_2025 == 0 | is.na(n_la_2025)) &
           !(n_core_2025 == 0 | is.na(n_core_2025)))   %>%  # without la but with core
           select(tree, botanical, bota_code, label, dbh) %>%
  mutate(n_leaf = 5,
         n_wood = 0,
         type_sp = "compl_sp",
         type_ind = "compulsory") 
# then select the 8 bigger indiv per species not sampled as non compulsory
sampling_supl3.3 <- inventory %>%
  filter(botanical %in% supl3$botanical & 
           !(tree %in% c(sampling_supl3.1$tree, sampling_supl3.2$tree))) %>% 
  group_by(botanical) %>% 
  top_n(8, dbh) %>% 
  select(tree, botanical, bota_code, label, dbh) %>% 
  mutate(n_leaf = 5,
         n_wood = 2,
         type_sp = "compl_sp",
         type_ind = "optional") 
sampling_ind <- rbind(sampling_ind, sampling_supl1, sampling_supl2, sampling_supl3.1, sampling_supl3.2, sampling_supl3.3)  
```
